title: Why Habits Are So Hard to Break: The Brain's Reward Prediction Error
hook: Your brain likes being right, even about bad habits.

narration.text: Your brain likes being right, even about bad habits.
When you expect a reward, like a sugary snack, your brain releases dopamine.
If you get the snack, your brain updates its prediction for next time.
This is called the reward prediction error.
It reinforces the habit loop, making it stronger each time.
Breaking a habit means teaching your brain new predictions.
Replacing the old reward with a new, healthier one helps.
It takes time for your brain to learn the new pattern.
Which habits are you trying to change?

description: Ever wondered why some habits are so tough to ditch? It all comes down to your brain's reward system and something called the reward prediction error. Understanding this mechanism can help you finally break free from unwanted patterns.
topic: Why habits are so hard to break, explaining the reward prediction error.
